Personally, I have been training with AMEY SHARMA for 2 years now, and I couldn’t have asked for a better coach. He’s deeply involved not just in my workouts, but also in my diet, lifestyle, and overall fitness goals. On days that I’ve trained with other trainers, I’ve experienced the same professionalism - they instantly pick up from where Amey leaves off.

I can proudly say I’m a true fan of ANTI GRAVITY. I plan to continue setting new goals with them and achieving them too. They are growing and expanding rapidly, and this success is truly well deserved.

- Puneet Motiani

featured_reviews.name: Rylan Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been going to Golds Gym Bandra for many years since it opened, but only while visiting from the US. Initially I used to use the Golds gym “passport” but later started paying for 2 weeks at a time. I am used to it, so I kept coming back. I work out wherever I go in the world, and one of my favorite things to do when traveling is to try out the gym - whether it is a local gym or a hotel gym or a friends gym or a cruise ship gym. I’ve worked out in Sydney, Dubai, all over the US, in big cities and small towns, couple of gyms in Mumbai back in the day, many, many hotel gyms. So I’ve seen a fair bit of different gyms.

Let’s keep this simple and objective:

Pros
- Has all the strength training equipment you’d need for any body part
- Very helpful, friendly floor trainers for when you need a spot
- Ladies walking around with spray bottles who clean equipment off on request
- Very close to my mom’s place (where I grew up), just basically around the block, so very convenient for me
- People have good vibes - everyone is there to work out, not clown around. People do not hog machines. It is very acceptable to ask someone to rotate with you. In some gyms in other countries people want to plant themselves on a machine for 10-20-30 minutes, and think you are rude if you ask to work in with them (I’m just going 3 more sets!),
- 6 am to 12 midnight on weekdays, so not quite 24x7 but good number of hours

Cons
- Equipment, for the most part is the same stuff they opened with in 2003. This includes not just their machines, but their sound equipment. There are a couple of new things, but not that much.
- Speaking of sound equipment, they have some random music playing each time I visit. Sometimes it’s rap, sometimes club, sometimes goodness knows what. And it is always very loud.
- Lots. Of. People. It is very crowded, all the time. And either their A/C does not work, or it is so crowded all you feel is sweaty body heat from everyone. Luckily, because members are SO good about rotating between sets, you can use any machine you want with only a 30 second wait usually. What this means is you also need to be comfortable with rotating with other people. You can’t just leave your stuff on a bench and go chat with someone.
- Very few cardio machines, and it is too hot to run anyway.

As a bonus, here are some interesting stats.
- One gym I go to in Wisconsin is about 40x as big as Golds gym. Hard to believe, but it’s true. Also since there are so many people there, and they DONT rotate machines like at Golds gym, I prefer Golds gym.
- One gym I go to is about 2-3 times as big as Golds gym. But there are not many people there at any point in time. That’s my favorite place to work out, because I can get a good solid work out in and it is quiet and pretty empty all the time.  They also got all new equipment recently.

Anyway, the moral of the story is -
Golds Gym Bandra is a decent gym for serious weight training, with aging yet adequate equipment, and excellent floor trainers. It is always stuffy and crowded, but members make up for this with good gym etiquette, freely letting other members rotate within sets. While there are way bigger and better gyms around the world, with more modern equipment, it does not necessarily mean you will enjoy your workout more elsewhere!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I took one year membership and i hardly went to the gym.

Before my wedding i took personal training.

During one of the sessions, one other trainer threw a bench at us, it hit both me as well my trainer. I was in shock as i had never even seen that person earlier maybe the trainers had some rivalry or something i still have no clue.

I went to the gym management immediately and they did nothing and i was hit, i was lucky it hit my leg but it could have been my head as earlier i was lying down and doing another variation and i had my wedding in 15 days.

I kept insisting them to take action but they did nothing i waited for almost an hour after my workout was disturbed then finally i had to call the police on 100 and the cops came and took both me and the trainer who assaulted me  in a van, i had never sat in one in my life, and my trainer also came later to give his side of the story as even he was hit by the bench, even on the way the other trainer abused a lot and threatened with dire consequences, they sent me for medical at baba hospital and then i submitted everything and left but no action was taken as the cop said the gym owner is an influential person.

No one from the gym management did anything they even told the cops it’s another trainer who did it and they can’t be held responsible for it hence no complaint can be filed against them.

I had 6 months of my membership left but it didn’t feel like it’s a safe place because management did nothing they didn’t even provide the footage of the person throwing the bench even when there is a cctv in the gym and he kept abusing me and laughing when ever i went to the gym after this happened, i was a paying customer at the gym and he was just a trainer and management did nothing.

After I complained, when ever i went to the gym the valet handed me over the keys never got the car back to gate and one of the time the car tyres were flat that’s when i decided on leaving the gym and i had to discontinue the personal training also.

The gym was really good and equipment is good also and they have everything you need except a 45Degree leg press, good crowd, there is valet parking service as well, it’s also the most VFM gym in the area, building is really bad in terms of cleanliness, there are cockroaches everywhere because there are lot of eateries, gym was super clean though but what happened came as a shock to me and i never went back even for a single day even though i had 6 months remaining on my membership subscription because safety was an issue, what if the guy hit the bench on my head while i was working out while lying down how would i protect myself, so you can imagine the trauma and no one goes to the gym to fight, in-fact i am always running short on time so I don’t even interact much i just leave as soon as i am done. Those days i was preparing for my wedding so i had 1000 things to do and they troubled me at that time so you can imagine what’s the mentality of the gym managment.

For me to go to the police station and then medical examination at baba hospital was like trauma because ideally the managment should have taken action, instead of compelling me to call the cops and my whole day was wasted i had to skip my clothes trial fitting appoint that day i remember and you also get unnecessarily stressed.

When i had joined the gym they made me read a lengthy document on gym rules but their trainer didn’t follow the same and they did nothing at all.

I am paying exactly double the amount per person  i paid at 360 but i am at peace when i work out at the current gym, there is no security concern or threat.

my personal trainer was outstanding he made me achieve my goal of looking fit for my wedding in less than a month i could have gotten better as this incident spoiled our momentum and discontinued, he even came to the police station with me and narrated the truth to them.

So if anything happens in the gym, management will do nothing they will shrug off any responsibility or accountability so please keep this in mind before joining.

featured_reviews.name: Jasmine K

What a wild 8-month fitness journey in Bombay!

I signed up for the 72 + 1 free class package at Flofit while I was in India — honestly thinking I’d never finish it. I walked in with a bunch of health issues and zero energy, plus those chaotic Bombay monsoons made getting to the gym feel like a mini survival challenge 😂. I cancelled so many times in the beginning… but slowly, I found my rhythm, pushed through, and I actually completed the entire package! 🙌

Flofit is such a vibe — great music, solid energy, and all the latest equipment. Big thanks to Wasim, who convinced me to take the plunge and always greets everyone with that trademark smile. And Shrutika, who’s the sweetest and never misses saying hi and bye.

My biggest shoutout goes to Sujit, my trainer — truly the best. Kind, funny, and incredibly patient. He’s super attentive and really focuses on mobility, stretches, and form. I always looked forward to my PT sessions with him — we had great chats and lots of laughs. I’m going to miss him the most. Highly recommend Sujit if you’re looking for a top-notch coach!

Special mention to Mahesh and the entire Flofit crew — sorry if I’ve missed a few names, you guys are all awesome.

Now that I’m heading back to Singapore, I can proudly say I feel stronger, healthier, and more alert. All my health markers are down — mission accomplished 💪

The programming is balanced enough that you can go every day if you want, and still benefit. From Monday to Friday here are six classes from 6am to noon, and another four from 5pm to 8pm in the  evening, so the schedule is really flexible and you can go to any class that suits. The gym is also open for solo workouts or personal training at the weekend.

The only thing I would change is to recommend purchasing air purifiers for the gym space, to protect clients' and staff members' health once monsoon ends. I think this was considered before and it would be a good investment.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Five Gardens area in Matunga is part of the famous Dadar-Parsi colony. This area was specially established for the upper class Parsis in the very early 19th century by the efforts of Mancherji Edalji Joshi, a renowned Parsi patron. The British however built it under the scheme of Bombay City Improvement Plan for the localities of Dadar, Matunga, Wadala, Sion in 1899-1900. So this is the first planned area of the city with spaces allocated for residences, green space, schools and colleges with proximity to transport infrastructure
The purpose was to de-congest the city after the Bombay Bubonic Plague Epidemic which broke in the September of 1896. According to the plan they wanted to house about 60,000 people in Sion and about 85,000 in Dadar & Matunga. Now there is as much people in every square kilometer of this area
So back to the garden itself. These are exactly five gardens just like shown in the map above. Getting here is quite simple. This is at a walking distance from King’s Circle and if you take the train get down at either Matunga or King’s Circle Railway Station and then take the taxi.
The garden itself is like any other Government infrastructure waiting to fall apart.
